Y.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage curriculum for sparse-reward reinforcement learning: a dense-reward shaping pretraining stage followed by sparse-reward fine-tuning with a KL constraint. Experiments on MiniGrid mazes report 2.3× sample-efficiency improvement.

strengths.comment: The two-stage dense-to-sparse curriculum is well-motivated and aligned with reverse-curriculum prior work.
The hypothesis in the Introduction is clearly framed and tied to falsifiable experimental claims.

weaknesses.comment: The Conclusion claims the KL constraint is 'critical' but provides no ablation that varies the KL weight; the criticality claim therefore rests on prior work rather than the paper's own evidence.
weaknesses.evidence_grounding: arXiv:2105.99999 (Constraint-Free Policy Distillation Fails on Harder Targets) plus absence of in-paper ablation.

questions.question: Was a partially-frozen encoder ablated as an intermediate design between full freezing and full fine-tuning?
